name: Walking Truck
def: Hydraulic four legged vehicle from General Electric that an operator drove by moving his own arms and legs inside a force feedback harness.
body: Built for the US Army by Ralph Mosher at General Electric, the Walking Truck was a rideable quadruped meant to carry loads over ground that wheels could not cross. Each leg had three hydraulically powered joints, and the driver commanded them through a master slave linkage that fed contact forces back to his own hands and feet. Operators could walk the machine, step over obstacles and lift heavy objects with a leg, but the control scheme was so tiring that the project ended after trials.
facts: Built under the US Army Cybernetic Anthropomorphous Machine programme
Could lift loads of several hundred kilograms with a single leg
Preserved at the US Army Transportation Museum at Fort Eustis
specs: Hydraulic cylinders, three powered joints per leg
Onboard internal combustion engine driving hydraulic pumps
None, direct human force feedback teleoperation
